ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a coordinate plane; a straight line slanting downward to the right intersects the x-axis at point A, and A is to the left of the origin O; it intersects the y-axis at point B, and B is below the origin O. Point C is in the second quadrant, and a horizontal line segment is drawn from C to the right to the y-axis, with the foot of the perpendicular being D; in the figure CD is perpendicular to the y-axis. Then reason: Because CD is perpendicular to the y-axis and CD=4, CD represents the horizontal distance from point C to the y-axis; and C is in the second quadrant, so x_C=-4. Substitute x=-4 into the line y=-3/2 x-2, obtaining y=6-2=4, so C=(-4,4). Point A is the intersection point of the line and the x-axis; let y=0, then 0=-3/2 x-2, solving gives x=-4/3, so A=(-4/3,0). To make P be on the y-axis and make PA+PC shortest, reflect A about the y-axis to A'=(4/3,0), then PA=PA', so PA+PC=P A'+PC. When A', P, and C are collinear, the sum of distances is shortest. The slope of line A'C is (4-0)/(-4-4/3)=4/(-16/3)=-3/4. The equation of the line passing through A'(4/3,0) is y=-3/4(x-4/3)=-3/4 x+1. When it intersects the y-axis, x=0, obtaining y=1, therefore P=(0,1).

method.method_draft: First describe/read the figure: the diagram shows a coordinate plane with a decreasing straight line crossing the x-axis at A to the left of O and the y-axis at B below O; point C lies in quadrant II, and CD is drawn horizontally from C to the y-axis. From the text, use CD perpendicular to the y-axis and CD=4, so the horizontal distance from C to the y-axis is 4; since C is in quadrant II, x_C=-4. Substitute into the given line y=-3/2 x-2 to get C=(-4,4). Also get A from the x-intercept of the line: 0=-3/2 x-2, so A=(-4/3,0). To minimize PA+PC with P constrained to the y-axis, reflect A across the y-axis to A'=(4/3,0). Then PA=A'P, so PA+PC=A'P+PC is minimized when A', P, C are collinear. Find the intersection of line A'C with the y-axis: the slope from A'(4/3,0) to C(-4,4) is -3/4, so at x=0 the y-value is 1. Therefore P=(0,1).

method.method_draft: First describe/read the figure: the image shows P must lie somewhere on the y-axis between the general vertical positions of A and C, with A on the x-axis left of O and C in quadrant II connected horizontally to the y-axis by CD. From the text and figure, CD=4 is a horizontal distance to the y-axis; since C is in quadrant II, x_C=-4. Put x=-4 into y=-3/2x-2 to obtain C=(-4,4). The x-intercept of the line gives A=(-4/3,0). Let P=(0,t) on the y-axis. Then PA+PC equals sqrt((0+4/3)^2+(t-0)^2)+sqrt((0+4)^2+(t-4)^2). Minimize f(t)=sqrt(16/9+t^2)+sqrt(16+(t-4)^2). Differentiate and set f'(t)=0: t/sqrt(16/9+t^2)+(t-4)/sqrt(16+(t-4)^2)=0. Solving gives t=1, and this gives the minimum because the sum of distances to two fixed points as a function along a line is convex. Hence P=(0,1).
